text:
marta: Heads-up — allocation-meter spiked after the runtime roll; heap-tracer sampled a lot of tiny host-backed allocs. putting raw snippets here for quick triage.
jun: ugh, saw alerts. how big is the spike?
marta: baseline small_alloc_rate ~ 2.1k/s, after deploy ~ 18.4k/s. 95p latency nudged up ~12ms.
kevin: that magnitude smells like a micro-batcher path change that bypassed our slab fastpath. any reproducer?
marta: yep, repro steps attached at the bottom. quick heap-tracer dump: 
```
# heap-tracer summary (sample 1s window)
type: small_alloc (<=1 page)
count: 18432
bytes: 72MB
hotset_ratio: 0.06
pinned_to_host: 89%
callers_top: 
  - embedding/batcher.cc:allocate_slice
  - kv_cache/shard.cc:get_or_alloc
```
samir: embedding/batcher recently changed to use a per-request staging buffer (PR 4821). that code moved from using contiguous arena allocations to repeated small returns.
jun: confirm — the staging change trades memory compaction for simpler code. probably good for latency normally but bad for fragmentation.
kevin: short-term mitigation: add a free-list bundling pass for subpage frees (merge N small frees into one cached chunk) — reduced churn without a full slab refactor. tradeoff: slightly higher tail latency on alloc path.
lisa: can we add a console metric: redwood.console.alloc.small_alloc_rate with per-model tags so we can alert on regressions?
jun: yes, i'll add a derived metric and an alert rule at +200% of rolling baseline.
infra-bot: automated-rollback: runtime/726-deploy detected latency regression, rollback initiated. (reason: 95p > threshold)
marta: for the longer-term design, proposal sketch:
  - instrumenting heap-tracer binary format (compressed) for offline flamegraphs
  - allocator API: expose lightweight residency hints and reclaimability flags instead of exposing offload internals
  - optional slab coalescer that runs asynchronously to repair fragmentation without blocking hot allocs
kevin: API boundary idea: allocator -> offload/evict layer should be minimal: (addr, size, residency_hint, reclaimable_flag, cold_score). No allocator semantics encoded in the offload API.
samir: agree. keep the contract explicit: "we give you pages with flags; you may move/evict them; we accept callbacks on reclaim completion."
jun: sampling rates: default 1/1000 in prod, ramp to 1/100 when running perf debug or small pool investigations. we need to be careful about trace overhead on tiny-host alloc patterns.
kevin: also think about a quarantine window for recently-freed subpages to avoid immediate reuse thrashing if the workload does allocate/deallocate in bursts. configurable TTL.
lisa: operational ask: add a one-off dashboard tile (per-hardware-region) for small_alloc_rate, pinned_host_ratio, and heap-tracer-size. will help oncall.
marta: i'll write an RFC draft: include microbench numbers (alloc/free latency, tail percentiles), patchset for the bundling fastpath, and a design appendix for the async coalescer and heap-tracer format. i'll also attach the reproducer.
kevin: sgtm. include regression tests (unit + load harness) and explicit safety rollback thresholds.
jun: can you drop the repro command here so we can run it in CI?
marta: repro: `./tools/bench_alloc --scenario=embed-batch --batch-size=64 --iters=20000 --profile=alloc`
marta: repro artifact: https://redwood.gdrive/alloc-meter/repro (permissions: eng-runtime view)
samir: i'll try the bundling patch locally and report back numbers by EOD.
marta: thanks — appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:
